facts.statement: ffmpeg here can encode H.264 + AAC (and VP9/Opus, AV1, HEVC); drawtext, subtitles/libass and zoompan filters exist
facts.evidence: ffmpeg 6.1.1-3ubuntu5. `ffmpeg -encoders`: libx264, libx265, libvpx, libvpx-vp9, libaom-av1, libsvtav1, aac, libopus, libmp3lame, libvorbis. `-filters`: drawtext, subtitles, ass, zoompan, flite. My proof clip uses libx264+aac+drawtext+zoompan and decodes cleanly (`ffmpeg -i proof_burned.mp4 -f null -` OK).

facts.statement: Fonts for drawtext/burned captions are available
facts.evidence: fc-list: 103 faces. Inter (all weights, OTF, /usr/share/fonts/opentype/inter/), DejaVu Sans/Serif/Mono, Liberation, Carlito, FreeSans, Noto Color Emoji, WenQuanYi. The site itself ships Inter and Bricolage Grotesque woff2 in docs/assets/fonts, but those are woff2 and drawtext needs TTF/OTF, so use the system Inter OTF for burned text. Burned caption in proof used Inter-SemiBold.otf and renders correctly (burned_frame.png).

facts.statement: Playwright recordVideo of a scripted page interaction at 1280x720 works in this container
facts.evidence: Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1194/chrome-linux/chrome, Playwright from /opt/node-tools/node_modules/playwright (node; the python module is not installed). Recorded 9.6 s scrolling home page then /apps/: VP8 webm, 1280x720, 25 fps, 240 frames, 885-921 kB (about 740 kbit/s raw); frame is not blank (mean 152, std 112). Limits: the cursor is not drawn, frame rate is fixed at 25 fps from screencast JPEG frames, and it only captures the page viewport (no browser chrome, no desktop). facts.statement: Encoded size of the 9.6 s Playwright recording, re-encoded to H.264
facts.evidence: CRF28 preset slow: 413,049 B = 344 kbit/s; CRF23: 624,930 B = 521 kbit/s; `-b:v 1M -maxrate 1M`: 871,081 B = 726 kbit/s (the cap is not binding for static-ish web content).

facts.statement: Size estimate for a 120 s 1280x720 screen-content video
facts.evidence: Measured on 20 s of continuous slow zoom over the Welcome_Notebook.png still (the worst realistic 'Ken Burns' content), then x6: CRF28 = 1,009,535 B = 404 kbit/s -> about 6.1 MB; CRF23 = 777 kbit/s -> about 11.7 MB; 1 Mbit/s cap = 937 kbit/s -> about 14.1 MB (hard ceiling 15 MB for 120 s). Scrolling-site recording extrapolates to 5.2 MB (CRF28), 7.8 MB (CRF23), 10.9 MB (1M ABR). Static holds cost almost nothing (40 kbit/s -> 0.6 MB per 120 s). 1080p CRF28 with zoom = 551 kbit/s -> about 8.3 MB. Add audio: AAC 64 kbit/s = 0.96 MB per 120 s (Opus 48k = 0.7 MB). Planning number: 7-9 MB for a 720p CRF28 narrated video, 10 MB if 1080p, below 16 MB in every case. Caveat: dense motion (napari redraws, scrolling long notebooks) will cost more than these samples.

facts.statement: A pitfall in ffmpeg zoompan
facts.evidence: With `-loop 1 -t N` the zoompan option d must be 1 (and use `in` not `on` for the counter), otherwise each input frame yields d output frames: my first attempt with d=500 ran away to a multi-MB, effectively endless output and had to be killed. Correct form: `-loop 1 -framerate 25 -t 20 -i img.png -vf "scale=2560:-2,zoompan=z='1+0.0004*in':x='iw/2-(iw/zoom/2)':y='ih/4-(ih/zoom/4)':d=1:s=1280x720:fps=25,format=yuv420p"` (about 14 s to render 20 s). Upscaling a 1826x834 screenshot to 2560 wide looks soft (poster.jpg): real captures must be taken at 2x device scale or at least 1920 px wide for zooms.

facts.statement: Burned-in versus sidecar captions both work; WebVTT <track> works in Chromium
facts.evidence: proof/proof_burned.mp4 (drawtext, 354,445 B, 5 s) and proof/proof_clean.mp4 + proof/proof.vtt. Headless Chromium test (proof/play.js): `<video><source webm><track kind=captions src=proof.vtt default></video>` gives textTracks=1, cues=1, activeCues=1 after 1.5 s of playback, and the video played with no error.

facts.statement: Playwright's Chromium can play the H.264 MP4
facts.evidence: In the same test `canPlayType('video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E, mp4a.40.2"')` returned '' while webm vp9/opus returned 'probably'. The bundled Chromium has no proprietary codecs. So 'MP4 plays' cannot be proven in this container's browser; verify with ffprobe/ffmpeg decode here and on real Chrome/Firefox/Safari/phone by a human. Serving both <source> types (MP4 first, optional VP9 WebM) is possible; the VP9 version of the 5 s proof is 397 kB.

facts.statement: Poster extraction works
facts.evidence: `ffmpeg -ss 2.5 -i proof_clean.mp4 -frames:v 1 -q:v 3 poster.jpg` produced a 77,672 B 1280x720 JPEG.

facts.statement: Offline text-to-speech is available in this container
facts.evidence: No espeak-ng, piper, pico2wave, festival, flite binaries. But (a) ffmpeg has the libflite filter: `ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "flite=text='...':voice=slt"` works with no install, 0.3 s for 4.4 s of audio, robotic (voices kal, slt, rms, awb); (b) `pip` works through the proxy: piper-tts 1.8.0 (wheel 34 MB, bundles espeak-ng-data and onnxruntime, installed in a venv in scratch, not system) plus voices downloaded from huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices (en_US-lessac-medium 63 MB, en_US-libritts_r-medium 78 MB). Piper runs on 4 CPUs in 2.4 s (lessac, 3.8 s of audio) and 7 s (libritts_r, includes model load), so a 120 s narration renders in well under a minute. Speech rate: lessac 11 words in 3.82 s (about 173 wpm), libritts_r 11 words in 3.20 s: a 120 s script is about 300-340 words. I could not listen to audio; the files are not silent (mean -19.1 dB, peak 0 dB in the muxed clip) but naturalness is unassessed (unverified by ear).

facts.statement: Licences of the TTS options
facts.evidence: piper-tts 1.8.0 METADATA: GPL-3.0-or-later (OHF-voice/piper1-gpl): fine for a build-time tool, its audio output is not a derivative work, but do not vendor it into the site repo. Voice cards (huggingface rhasspy/piper-voices MODEL_CARD): libritts_r = CC BY 4.0 (needs attribution, 904 speakers), ljspeech/high = public domain, alba (en_GB) = CC BY 4.0, hfc_female = CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (avoid), amy = 'See URL' (unclear). lessac = Blizzard 2013 'Research Licence Agreement' (www.cstr.ed.ac.uk/projects/blizzard/2013/lessac_blizzard2013/license.html: licence granted only to a named person/organisation after a form, research licence): do NOT use it for published narration. Recommended: en_US-ljspeech-high (public domain) or en_US-libritts_r-medium (CC BY 4.0, credit in transcript/page footer). flite voices are CMU/BSD-style, permissive, lowest quality.

facts.statement: napari can be run in this container
facts.evidence: napari 0.9.2 + PyQt5 installed OK in a venv (scratch/napari-test/venv) but `napari.Viewer(show=True)` aborts: under xvfb the Qt xcb plugin cannot load (`libxcb-icccm.so.4: cannot open shared object file`; further libxcb-* likely); `apt-get download` fails (no package index) and I did not run apt-get update/install on the system. With QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen or vnc it gets past Qt but vispy fails (`glGetParameter ... NoneType has no attribute decode`, no OpenGL context even with LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1). So napari screenshots/screencasts need a human desktop (or a root install of the libxcb-* packages plus mesa, untested). The Tools protocol itself warns of this error: HUMAN_TEST_PROTOCOL.md says 'On a very bare Linux system Napari may also need the libxcb-* system packages'.

facts.statement: Real build/release sequence and names
facts.evidence: Docs order (README.md): Before getting started; Create repository ('Use this template' > 'Create a new repository'); Enable automatic template updates (one-time secret/token); Initialise (labconstrictor-form.streamlit.app, 'Start initialisation' in 'Initialise a repository' -> Pull Request to accept); Customise installer images; Describe your app for the App Centre; Upload external code (optional); Generate requirements; Upload notebooks (same web form, 'Upload/Update notebook', 'Validate submission', then 'Create pull request', needs a personal access token, PR is merged and a workflow validates and may auto-revert); Create installers (Releases > 'Create a new release', tag must be semver e.g. 0.0.1, 'Publish release'; check Actions tab first, no workflow running); Install an app. release_constructor.yml: trigger release published or workflow_dispatch; matrix linux (ubuntu-latest), macos-arm64 (macos-15), macos-intel (macos-15-intel), windows (windows-latest).

facts.statement: Installers and platforms
facts.evidence: before_getting_started.md: Windows (.exe), macOS (.pkg), Linux (.sh), built with Conda Constructor. NucleiSky 0.1.1 release (7 Jul 2026) actually holds 7 files: Linux-x86_64.sh; MacOSX-arm64.pkg and .sh; MacOSX-x86_64.pkg and .sh; Windows-x86_64.exe and .msi; each 190-318 MB. install.md: installation takes 6-8 minutes, installers are not code-signed (Windows 'More info' > 'Run anyway'; macOS 'Open Anyway'), a command prompt window opens on Windows, Linux needs `bash file.sh`. facts.statement: Manifest filename labconstrictor-app.yaml and its content
facts.evidence: app_manifest.md: file at the repository root, read by the App Centre; required keys per schema (.tools/schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json): schema, name, summary, kind (analysis, segmentation, simulation, game, training, utility), distribution (at least one of installer: true, colab: [{label,url}], pip). Optional: description, quickstart, hosts (notebook, napari, fiji, qupath), authors, license, categories, doi, homepage, docs_url, icon, screenshots. There is NO 'citation' field: the paper is `doi` (NucleiSky: 10.1242/jcs.265152) and documentation is `docs_url`. Having the file does not list the app: author must submit the repo at labconstrictor.cellmig.org/submit/; a private repo cannot be listed. The initialiser adds the file to the init PR. Check App Centre manifest workflow only warns when missing.

findings:
TOOLING (all measured in this container)
- Works: ffmpeg 6.1.1 with libx264, aac, libvpx/vp9, libopus, drawtext, subtitles(libass), zoompan, flite. Inter OTF fonts are installed for drawtext. Playwright (node, /opt/node-tools, Chromium 1194) recordVideo at 1280x720 gives 25 fps VP8 webm, about 740 kbit/s, no cursor. Poster extraction and WebVTT <track> work. A 5 s proof pipeline exists in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/a3a6ac4f-1857-5992-b7c5-06332778d500/scratchpad/demo-feasibility/video/proof/: proof_burned.mp4 (burned caption), proof_clean.mp4 + proof.vtt + proof_clean.webm (sidecar captions, cue shown in Chromium), poster.jpg, narr_lessac.wav/narr_libritts.wav/narr_flite.wav, est* size-estimate clips. It combines a zoompan over the Welcome notebook still, a Piper narration, AAC audio and a burned or sidecar caption.
- Size model for the 120 s 720p video (measured, extrapolated): CRF28 about 5-6 MB video; CRF23 about 8-12 MB; 1 Mbit/s cap at most 15 MB (measured 11-14 MB for motion content); 1080p CRF28 about 8 MB; plus 0.7-1.0 MB audio. Plan: 720p, CRF 26-28, AAC 64k, `-movflags +faststart`, expect 7-9 MB, hard cap 15 MB. Repo/pages impact is about +8 MB in site/ (now 23 MB) and about +8 MB git history per re-render.
- Playwright Chromium cannot play H.264 (canPlayType mp4 = ''), so 'MP4 plays' must be verified with ffprobe/ffmpeg decode here and in real browsers by a human; optionally also ship a VP9 WebM <source>.
- TTS: nothing preinstalled except ffmpeg's flite (robotic). pip works: piper-tts 1.8.0 (GPL-3.0-or-later, build-time only; keep out of the site repo) with voices from huggingface. Licence-safe voices: en_US-ljspeech-high (public domain), en_US-libritts_r-medium (CC BY 4.0; credit it), en_GB-alba (CC BY 4.0). Avoid en_US-lessac (Blizzard research licence) and hfc_female (NC). Synchronise captions by generating TTS per sentence, measuring each WAV duration with ffprobe and writing the VTT from those durations. I could not judge naturalness by ear.
- Headless GUI apps: Fiji runs headless (macro) and in Xvfb with x11grab capture (about 50 s start, no window manager); the LabConstrictor Fiji command itself was not run. napari does not run: PyQt5 xcb plugin fails on missing libxcb-icccm4 (and probably other libxcb libs), and without xcb there is no OpenGL context for vispy; I did not apt-install. Real napari and Fiji screenshots already exist in LabConstrictor-Tools docs/img and show the fixture.
- Must be done by a human: record or approve narration (or accept Piper), capture authenticated or desktop screens (GitHub Use this template / Releases / Assets, the Streamlit form with a PAT, Colab, installer dialogs on Windows/macOS, a real installed app launch with its terminal window, JupyterLab with NucleiSky2DApp, a real napari and Fiji session with the plugin), listen to the audio, play the MP4 on real browsers and a phone, and decide on the voice licence.
- Scratch folder is 2.8 GB (Fiji zip 700 MB plus unpacked, napari venv, 2 Piper voices) left from a previous attempt of this task; delete after use. The local clones are stale (template at 13 Aug); the facts above come from origin/main via git fetch (read-only).

TRUTH OF THE STORYBOARD: sentence by sentence (storyboard in ideas-demo-and-video.md lines 23-33)
1. 0-12 s 'reference, query crop, successful registration overlay': fine, but show the fixture or a real run and quote provenance; the NucleiSky 2D_QC.jpg is a separate illustrative result.
2. 12-30 s 'build a reusable scientific API (src/ Python package ...)': correct as design advice; the template step is 'Upload external code (optional)' (src/<PROJ>/ with __init__.py, upload through GitHub). Wording: 'put reusable code in a normal Python package under src/; notebooks import it'. 'Callable from another program' is true for NucleiSky (pip: nucleisky).
3. 30-49 s 'same notebook in Google Colab and JupyterLab, real ipywidgets controls': true for NucleiSky (@title, google.colab guard, ipywidgets, colab links in the manifest). Technical point list 'per the real guide ... explicit versioned dependencies' is IMPRECISE: the portability guide does not cover versioned dependencies; say 'pinned versions in requirements.yaml (notebook_requirements.md)'.
4. 49-65 s 'package with LabConstrictor (GitHub template, notebook upload, requirements.yaml; transition into the Welcome notebook)': imprecise. Correct: create a repository from the template, enable automatic template updates (one-time), initialise through the web form (Start initialisation, accept the pull request), generate a requirements.yaml per notebook (Requirements Generator notebook), upload with 'Upload/Update notebook' in the same form (opens a pull request that you merge; needs a personal access token). 'Include reusable modules' is an optional earlier step, not after upload.

Zoompan on small screenshots is soft (a 1826 px wide capture scaled to 2560) and a continuous zoom costs about 400 kbit/s; low-res captures will look blurry on a 1080p or retina display. Capture at 2x and use cropping or short holds.

H.264 cannot be tested in the bundled Chromium; playback must be tested by a human on real browsers/phones, and the preview server (python http.server) lacks Range support so seeking behaviour is untested.
